newsitem.title: UK: Nikko Europe expands its financial products group.
newsitem.headline: Nikko Europe expands its financial products group.

text.p: Nikko Europe Plc, the European investment banking arm of Nikko Securities Co Ltd said it has made several new appointments within its Financial Products Group to develop proprietary trading products for Nikko.
The new recruits will take up their posts on a variety of start dates over the next two months.

The group, jointly headed by Frederic Robert and Hiroshi Wakutsu, was formed earlier this year to focus on arbitrage and relative value trades in addition to a range of structured and derivative based products.
It is already active in equity financing, equity options and arbitrage and is being strengthened with the addition of a quatitative research team and expanding its equity financing team.
Bruno Dupire will head the new quatitative research team and will be responsible for building up the analytics and risk analysis tools for Nikko on a global basis.

Dupire, joins from Paribas Capital Markets where he was head of derivatives research over the past four years. With two colleagues, he developed the "Smile Model" -- also known as the Dupire-Derman-Rubinstein model -- which is used for pricing and hedging exotic and European options.
Also joining the research team from Paribas Capital Markets are Guillaume Blacher, an equity derivatives quant specialist, and Antoine Savine, a fixed income quant specialist.
The equity financing group will be headed by Christophe Reech who is joining from Commerz Financial Products in Frankfurt where he was global head of equity financing for the past two years.
Also joining from Commerz Financial Products are three equity finance traders, Bastian Cohen, Bisera Regenstein and Frederic Dommart.

Simon James is also joining Nikko to provide a dedicated front-office IT resource to the Financial Products Group. He joins from HSBC Markets where he was a systems development manger for the past three years for the interest rate, equity indices and foreign exchange structured derivatives business.

"We now have the platform to build a very strong global derivatives and structured finance business to add to our strengths in capital markets, equity and fixed income," said Michel de Carvalho, joint chairman of Nikko Europe in a statement.
